events.text: Your father is heading out to the fields before dawn. "Coming, little one?"

choices.text: Trot along beside him all morning.
Ask to carry the seed basket.
Stay home with your mother instead.

events.text: A column of soldiers marches through on the kingdom road, spears catching the light.

choices.text: Stand at attention and salute as they pass.
Hide behind your mother's skirts.
Ask one of them what it's like to fight.

events.text: A merchant caravan rolls into the village square, wheels creaking under bolts of cloth and clay jars.

choices.text: Help unload a crate for a copper coin.
Stare at all the strange goods from far away.
Try to swipe a sweet when no one's looking.

events.text: By the hearth, an old traveler tells of the Rifts, doors to other worlds where the laws of nature bend.

choices.text: Listen wide-eyed, begging for more.
Ask if the stories are really true.
Fall asleep before the story ends.

events.text: A hunter drags a strange, faintly glowing carcass through the square. A crowd gathers.

choices.text: Push to the front to look closely.
Look away, a little scared.
Ask the hunter a hundred questions.

events.text: Today is a festival: drums, dancing, and honeyed cakes fill the square.

choices.text: Dance until you're dizzy.
Sneak a second helping of cake.
Watch from the edge of the crowd.

events.text: A noble's carriage rolls through, banners snapping, guards at every corner.

choices.text: Wave and cheer with the crowd.
Wonder what it's like to live in a castle.
Scowl at the guards keeping everyone back.

events.text: The smithy's hammer rings out; sparks fly bright against the dark forge.

choices.text: Watch, transfixed, until your feet fall asleep.
Ask the smith to teach you something.
Try to sneak a touch of the hot iron.

events.text: You've wandered further than you're allowed, right up to where the trees close in dark and close.

choices.text: Take three steps into the shadow and dare yourself to stay.
Turn back before you're missed.
Collect a handful of pretty leaves and run home.

events.text: The chickens need feeding and the goat is hungry again.

choices.text: Feed them all without being asked twice.
Name every single chicken.
Chase the goat around the yard instead.

events.text: A village elder is teaching the local children their letters in the shade of the plaza.

choices.text: Sit still and learn every rune.
Draw pictures in the dirt instead of letters.
Ask endless questions until the elder sighs.

events.text: You broke something you shouldn't have, and your parents are not pleased.

choices.text: Own up right away.
Blame it on the wind.
Cry until they forget to be angry.

events.text: Your mother is baking bread and could use small, flour-covered hands.

choices.text: Knead the dough carefully, just as shown.
Eat more dough than you knead.
Ask why bread rises at all.

events.text: Rain drums on the roof all day; there's nothing to do but stay in.

choices.text: Listen to your parents' old stories.
Build a fort out of blankets and pretend to be a knight.
Practice your letters by the window.

events.text: A thin, half-wild kitten is hiding under the woodpile, hissing at everyone.

choices.text: Sit quietly until it trusts you enough to eat.
Try to grab it and end up scratched.
Leave it be; wild things belong wild.

events.text: The market stall has fresh honey oatcakes out to cool, unwatched for a moment.

choices.text: Take one without asking.
Wait patiently and ask nicely.
Offer to sweep the stall for a treat.

events.text: A storm rattles the shutters; thunder cracks close overhead.

choices.text: Run to your parents' bed.
Count the seconds between flash and thunder, fascinated.
Stand at the window and watch the lightning.

events.text: The village guard drills in the square, spears thumping in unison.

choices.text: Copy their stances with a stick for a spear.
Count how many mistakes they make.
Ask the sergeant if children can join.

events.text: A weary traveler passing through gives you a small trinket for helping carry their pack a way.

choices.text: Thank them and treasure it.
Ask where they've been and what they've seen.
Try to trade it for something better at the stall.

events.text: For one heart-pounding minute, you can't find your mother in the crowded market.

choices.text: Stand still and wait, just as you were taught.
Push through the crowd calling for her.
Follow the smell of the bakery to somewhere familiar.

events.text: Your family sings an old Caldric hearth-song after supper.

choices.text: Sing along as loud as you can.
Listen and learn every word by heart.
Make up your own silly verse.

events.text: The well bucket is heavy, but the house needs water for the evening.

choices.text: Carry it yourself, spilling half along the way.
Ask a passing villager to help.
Race another child to the well and back.

events.text: Someone mentions a toppled shrine in the western wood, moss-eaten and forgotten.

choices.text: Ask everyone you know about it.
Decide you'll go looking for it yourself one day.
Shrug it off as an old tale.

events.text: Someone whittles you a toy bow. It's clumsy, but it's yours.

choices.text: Practice on a knot in the fence all afternoon.
Turn it into a game with the other children.
Take it apart to see how it works.

events.text: The whole village turns out for the harvest; even small hands are welcome.

choices.text: Work the fields until your back aches.
Organize the other children into a faster line.
Sneak off early to nap in the hay.

events.text: A travelling martial instructor offers to teach the village children a few real stances, for a fee.

choices.text: Beg your parents for the coin.
Watch from the fence and copy for free.
Decide fighting isn't for you.

events.text: Word spreads that bandits raided a farm on the edge of the region last night. The village is shaken.

choices.text: Ask the guard everything about what happened.
Help the frightened farm family however you can.
Lie awake imagining what you'd do if it happened here.

events.text: An adventurer limps into the village, bloodied but alive, muttering about something in the woods.

choices.text: Fetch the herbalist as fast as you can.
Ask them what they fought.
Stare at their strange, scorched gear.

events.text: A friend from the village hasn't been seen since yesterday. Everyone is worried.

choices.text: Join the search party, however small you are.
Check the forest edge where you two used to play.
Pray at the hearth for their safe return.

events.text: Half-buried at the edge of the wood, a smooth, faintly warm stone unlike any other you've seen.

choices.text: Pocket it and tell no one.
Bring it straight to the priest.
Leave it exactly where it lay.

events.text: During a festival blessing, the priest pauses over you a moment too long, murmuring something to themselves.

choices.text: Ask what they saw.
Pretend you didn't notice.
Tell your parents the moment you get home.

events.text: Another child your age keeps besting you at everything, on purpose, and loves rubbing it in.

choices.text: Train harder to beat them next time.
Laugh it off and befriend them instead.
Get even with a well-placed prank.

events.text: An older child has taken to shoving the younger ones around near the well.

choices.text: Stand between them and the younger children.
Report it to a parent or the guard.
Avoid the well until they lose interest.

events.text: Your family takes the cart to the nearest market town, a whole morning's ride away.

choices.text: Soak in every sight, sound and smell of a bigger place.
Watch the road the whole way for anything dangerous.
Haggle for a trinket yourself.

events.text: You're caught red-handed with a stolen apple in your pocket.

choices.text: Apologize and offer to work it off.
Run for it.
Claim you found it on the ground.

events.text: The older children are swimming in the river; it's time you learned too.

choices.text: Jump straight in, sputtering and laughing.
Watch carefully first, then try.
Stay on the bank; the water looks too cold.

events.text: The smith's apprentice needs an extra pair of hands pumping the bellows.

choices.text: Pump until your arms burn.
Ask to try striking the metal yourself.
Get distracted watching the sparks fly.

events.text: You find an old book tucked away that you're fairly sure you're not meant to read.

choices.text: Read it in secret by candlelight.
Ask a parent about it instead.
Put it back, a little spooked.

events.text: One of your parents is laid up sick in bed for days.

choices.text: Take over their chores without being asked.
Fetch the herbalist yourself.
Sit by the bed telling stories to keep their spirits up.

events.text: A runestone along the road flickers dim for a moment before steadying again. Nobody else seems to notice.

choices.text: Tell the guard captain right away.
Touch the stone, just to see.
Say nothing, unsure what you even saw.

events.text: Your father finally agrees to take you along on a short hunting trip.

choices.text: Track the prints exactly as he shows you.
Get impatient waiting in the blind.
Ask more questions than a hunt allows.

events.text: Something you made with your own hands actually sells at the market stall.

choices.text: Spend it all on sweets immediately.
Save it carefully in a tin under your bed.
Make another one right away, better this time.

events.text: The village keeps vigil through the solstice night, candles lit against the dark.

choices.text: Stay awake the whole night, proud of it.
Fall asleep against your mother's shoulder.
Count the candles instead of praying.

events.text: The other children dare you to go further into the wood than anyone your age has.

choices.text: Go further than anyone expects.
Go partway and turn back, calling it a win.
Refuse; it isn't worth the risk.

events.text: A minor noble tours the village and stops to ask the children their letters.

choices.text: Answer confidently, showing off a little.
Go shy and mumble your answer.
Ask the noble a bold question of your own.

events.text: A shoving match with another child turns into a real scrap before anyone pulls you apart.

choices.text: Stand your ground.
Try to talk your way out first.
Run and tell an adult instead.

events.text: The smith looks you over and grunts. "Strong arms. Ever thought about the forge?"

choices.text: Accept the apprenticeship.
Ask for a day to think it over.
Politely decline.

events.text: A neighboring farmer asks if you'd like steady work in the fields.

choices.text: Accept the work.
Ask about the pay first.
Say you have other plans.

events.text: A trader passing through offers to take you on as a cart hand and, if you're any good, an apprentice.

choices.text: Sign on for the road.
Ask your parents first.
Turn the offer down.

events.text: The Captain of the Guard mentions there's always room for a promising recruit once you're old enough.

choices.text: Say you'll be ready when the time comes.
Ask what training looks like.
Shrug it off for now.

events.text: The temple could use another pair of hands, the priest says, and perhaps more than that.

choices.text: Take up the temple work.
Help out without committing yet.
Decline; it isn't your calling.

events.text: A local hunter offers to teach you the trails, if you're willing to learn the hard way.

choices.text: Follow them into the wilds.
Ask to try it for a season first.
Say hunting isn't for you.

events.text: The herbalist notices your steady hands and asks if you'd like to learn the healing trade.

choices.text: Accept and start learning remedies.
Ask to see the healer's table first.
Decline for now.

events.text: A traveler in unfamiliar robes asks careful questions about you, then leaves a token with your parents.

choices.text: Keep the token close, curious.
Ask your parents what it means.
Hide it away and say nothing.

events.text: Word of your dual Blessing has clearly traveled further than the village; a stranger comes asking after you by name.

choices.text: Meet them and hear them out.
Avoid them entirely.
Tell the guard about the stranger.

events.text: With no Blessing to your name, most doors stay shut — but an odd, unaffiliated old wanderer seems to watch you with real interest.

choices.text: Approach the wanderer.
Keep your distance; you've had enough attention.
Ask around about who they are.
